correctness.rationale: For each of the seven transition types, explicit symbolic inversion reconstructs the formula for the payoff difference. An exact positive-semidefinite test ensures unique equilibrium, and positive component formulas characterize the admissible interior regime. Rational Bernstein coefficients certify the only nontrivial always-negative polynomial signs; derivative inequalities prove uniqueness of both positive threshold roots. The witness at beta=3/8 is checked with exact rational arithmetic, not floating-point approximations; standalone verify.py was executed successfully.

originality.rationale: The closest original model paper proves monotonicity of aggregate action or potential, not total individual equilibrium payoff, which is the squared Euclidean norm of the action vector. Related positive-spillover welfare bounds and centrality-key-player models neither state nor imply the sharp four-vertex classification. Two successful rounds of claim-specific published-record semantic searches and published-literature comparisons yielded no equal or stronger claim; this is evidence of supportable originality, not uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: Network design decisions often use the proven monotonicity of aggregate effort to predict outcomes. Here the distinct economically natural sum of private equilibrium profits moves in the opposite direction under a single edge. This analysis determines the sharp smallest network size, all first graph-edit types and two exact transition parameters, giving a structural boundary rather than a trivial reparameterization or one arbitrary numerical illustration.
